gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-gurmukh: Disorder looks raw and scattered, its crossbars as heavy as its stems and its glyphs set well apart. Noto Sans Gurmukhi follows in sans-serif form, with outward-pointing terminals and a lighter touch that gives the loud heading room to misbehave.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Rough, jumbled and unbothered, Disorder draws every stroke without any thick-to-thin shift, and its big lowercase looks ready to shout. And Noto Sans Hanunoo, sans-serif and open-ended, fills the line quietly beneath, leaving the heading font to do its work large and short.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads as a sans-serif with a deep midsection and wide gaps where curves meet stems. But Disorder pushes back with chaotic, widely spaced glyphs and crossbars as thick as its stems, so the page gets both a jolt and a rest.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic is a plain sans with open, pincer-like c shapes. Disorder is the better shouter, raw and jagged with every stroke at one weight, while the body font is better at settling into the line without a fuss.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian is a plain sans with big open eyes on its e and a, and a deep middle band. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian gives Disorder's chaotic, widely spaced capitals something sturdy to stand against.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-jp: Raw, loose and drawn like with a compass pencil, Disorder has a big lowercase that grabs the eye. Noto Sans JP, a plain sans with a very tall x-height and sweeping curves, supplies the steady counterweight.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Chaotic, with flat fineliner lines and glyphs set well apart, Disorder is the loud half. Noto Sans Kaithi fills the line with capital-sized lowercase and an open e, so the heading's mess lands against something sturdy and clear.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Chaotic like neon tubing bent into letters, Disorder never changes its thickness. Noto Sans Kannada, a plain sans with a gentle bump up to capitals and wide-open s curves, is the gentle foil that makes that wildness feel intentional.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-kayah-l: Noto Sans Kayah Li reads clean, its brush ends lifting away before curves close. Disorder, drawn with one tip and a rawness all its own, is the wild streak, and that gap between rough and tidy is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-kharosh: Disorder looks like twine pressed into a flat surface, chaotic and widely spaced, with big lowercase. But Noto Sans Kharoshthi counters with curves that never close and a dark stripe of lowercase, so the rawness above settles into something steady.
